title: Which free-time activity do most students like after playing?
description: A survey of one hundred and twenty students is drawn as a bar graph with one unit for five students. Dividing each count by five gives the bars, and the next tallest bar after playing shows the activity liked most after playing.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide each count by the scale to get the bar, then read the next tallest bar. Watch for students who name playing, the tallest bar, as the answer.

video_script.why: The child divides each count by a given scale to draw a bar graph, and reads the next tallest bar to answer a question.
video_script.substitution: Divide each count by five to get the bar heights, draw the bars, and find the tallest bar after playing.
video_script.anchor: the table of a survey of 120 students on free-time activity: playing 45, reading story books 30, watching TV 20, listening to music 10, painting 15
video_script.payoff_line: The bars are nine, six, four, two and three units tall

final_answer.value: bars of 9, 6, 4, 2 and 3 units; reading story books is liked most after playing
final_answer.spoken: the bars are nine, six, four, two and three units tall, and reading story books is liked most after playing

maths_rules: survey of 120 students: playing 45, reading story books 30, watching TV 20, listening to music 10, painting 15; 45 + 30 + 20 + 10 + 15 = 120
scale: 1 unit length = 5 students; the vertical line is marked 0 to 50 in jumps of 5
after playing (45), the next highest is reading story books (30)
video_script.design: One idea: divide each count by the scale, draw the bars, then read the next tallest bar. The table stays on the board all video and the bars rise beside it.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the table of the survey of 120 students: Playing 45, Reading story books 30, Watching TV 20, Listening to music 10, Painting 15, with small pictures of the activities

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.table: the table of five activities and their numbers of students appears with small pictures
marks.ask: an empty pair of lines appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about free time.
<bookmark mark='table'/>A survey asked one hundred and twenty students what they like to do in their free time.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Draw the bar graph, with one unit for five students. Which activity do most students like, other than playing?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a bar of 5 units labelled 25 students; the working 25 / 5 = 5; the label 1 unit length = 5 students

marks.label: the label 1 unit length = 5 students appears
marks.bar: a bar of five units appears and is labelled 25 students

narration: <bookmark mark='label'/>One unit of height stands for five students.
<bookmark mark='bar'/>A group of twenty five students needs a bar of five units.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>We get it by dividing twenty five by five.

beats.on_screen: Given: Playing 45, Reading story books 30, Watching TV 20, Listening to music 10, Painting 15; 1 unit length = 5 students

marks.first: Playing 45, Reading story books 30 and Watching TV 20 are written
marks.last: Listening to music 10 and Painting 15 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Given, forty five students like playing, thirty like reading, and twenty like watching television.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Ten like music, and fifteen like painting.

beats.on_screen: To find: the bar graph, and the activity liked most other than playing

marks.find: the words the bar graph and the activity liked most other than playing are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to draw the bar graph and find the next best activity.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw the two lines; write the five activities along the horizontal line; mark the vertical line 0, 5, 10 up to 50, one jump for each unit

marks.lines: a horizontal line and a vertical line are drawn and the five activities are written along the horizontal line
marks.axis: the vertical line is marked 0, 5, 10 and so on up to 50

narration: <bookmark mark='lines'/>Step one, draw the two lines and write the five activities along the bottom.
<bookmark mark='axis'/>Mark the side line in jumps of five, from zero up to fifty. The biggest count is forty five.
<bookmark mark='play'/>Step two, divide each count by five. Forty five divided by five is nine.
<bookmark mark='read'/>Thirty divided by five is six.
<bookmark mark='tv'/>Twenty divided by five is four.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 10 / 5 = 2; 15 / 5 = 3; the five bars of equal width are raised to 9, 6, 4, 2 and 3 units

marks.bars: the five bars of equal width rise to their heights

narration: <bookmark mark='music'/>Step three, finish the last two. Ten divided by five is two.
<bookmark mark='paint'/>Fifteen divided by five is three.
<bookmark mark='bars'/>Raise the five bars, all of equal width, to their heights.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: the tallest bar is playing, 9 units; leave it out, and the next tallest is reading story books, 6 units, taller than 4, 3 and 2

marks.next: the reading story books bar, 6 units, is lit as the tallest of the rest

narration: <bookmark mark='cover'/>Step four, playing is the tallest bar, so cover it.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Among the rest, the bar for reading is six units tall. The others are four, three and two.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check. 9 + 6 + 4 + 2 + 3 = 24 units; 24 x 5 = 120 students, the whole survey

marks.times: 24 x 5 = 120 is written and matches the survey

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step five, check the bars. Nine, six, four, two and three add up to twenty four units.
<bookmark mark='times'/>Twenty four times five is one hundred and twenty, which is the whole survey.

beats.on_screen: Answer: bars of 9, 6, 4, 2 and 3 units; reading story books is liked most after playing

marks.pay: the answer line is boxed and the five bars are labelled with their heights

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The bars are nine, six, four, two and three units tall. Reading story books is liked most after playing.
